title: Uniform and Lantern
premise: Hazel Okafor, indentured at fourteen to the Meridian Trading Company in the port city of Callow's Reach, has learned that history belongs to governors and merchants, never to divers' children. When a half-drowned stranger washes up with letters in the handwriting of Amara Voss — the reformist archivist officially executed two years ago — Hazel discovers the 'corpse' has been secretly documenting the Company's engineered famine, and the stranger is her courier. Pursued through three checkpoints by the Company's fixer, Silas Crane, Hazel must smuggle the archive to a sympathetic magistrate before the annual fleet departs and the evidence burns with it. At the last checkpoint Hazel chooses to surrender himself as a decoy so the papers pass, trading his freedom for the truth — and in the epilogue-tinged final scene, the famine inquiry opens with Hazel's name read aloud from the dockets, history finally happening to him, and because of him.
about_author: Lena Ashgrove is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial trading ledgers in West African and Caribbean port archives. She writes historical fiction about the people whose names the ledgers omitted.

chapters.title: Salt in the Ledger Ink
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. We see Callow's Reach through his careful invisibility: diving for pearls, memorizing which clerks take bribes, believing himself safely outside history. He witnesses a public flogging meant for a dockworker who asked about missing grain shipments. The beat is quiet dread — the reader sees what Hazel refuses to: he is already inside the story.

chapters.title: The Hand of a Drowned Woman
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A stranger, Tobias, collapses at the counting-house door clutching oilcloth-wrapped letters — unmistakably the hand of Amara Voss, whose execution Hazel watched the crowd celebrate. Tobias reveals the famine was engineered and begs Hazel's help reaching Magistrate Ferro before the fleet sails in six days. Beat: terror curdling into reluctant resolve.

chapters.title: Three Gates, One Lantern
chapters.summary: Alternating Hazel and Tobias POVs. The smuggling run through Callow's three checkpoints: bribery at the customs house, a near-miss at the garrison gate where Crane nearly recognizes Tobias, and betrayal at the harbor when a dockside friend sells them out. Crane captures Tobias; Hazel escapes with the papers but not the lantern that signals Ferro's boat. Beat: rising panic, sacrifice made real.

chapters.title: What the Fleet Carries
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, closing with a brief magistrate's record. At the final gate Hazel walks openly into Crane's custody as a decoy while Tobias, disguised in a diver's uniform, delivers the archive aboard Ferro's launch. Beaten in a cell, Hazel hears the fleet held by writ and the famine inquiry announced. Beat: grief transfigured — inheritance reclaimed, his name entered into history by his own hand.
